Alright, the last thing I did was fire off a tmux command that typed the request into the Glint REPL: 

```
write a detailed 400 word essay on terminal emulators, no file, just chat in your final answer
```

Then I gave the REPL a moment to start processing and captured the pane. The capture only showed the initial prompt and a blank input line—no essay content yet:

```
✦ glint v1.0.0 …
❯ write a detailed 400 word essay …
```

So the generation is still in progress. I need to wait until the model finishes streaming the essay before I try to capture the output again. 

I could just sleep for an arbitrary amount of time (e.g., 10 seconds) and then capture, but that would be brittle: if the essay takes longer, I’d miss the tail; if it finishes sooner, I’d waste time. The Glint UI has a built‑in indicator that appears when the stream is idle—specifically the line “esc to interrupt”. That string only shows up after the model has finished emitting output and is waiting for the next user command. Therefore I can use that as a reliable signal that the essay is complete.

The plan: repeatedly capture the pane and grep for that sentinel. As long as the sentinel is absent, sleep a short interval (say 3 seconds) and try again. Once the sentinel appears, break out of the loop. Then do a final capture of the pane, strip out any empty lines (so I only get the meaningful text), and show the last several lines of output. The essay will be long, and I only need to verify that it was generated and see the tail (the bottom part of the essay will be just above the input prompt). A `tail -14` should give me enough context to confirm the content without overwhelming the console.

Putting this together, the Bash one‑liner becomes:

```
until ! tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -q "esc to interrupt"; do sleep 3; done;
tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -14
```

The first part loops until the sentinel appears (`! … | grep -q` returns true when the pattern is found). The second part captures the pane, removes blank lines, and shows the final 14 lines, which should include the end of the essay and the prompt line. This will let me verify that the essay was indeed produced and that the docked layout (input at the bottom) is working as expected.

Thus the next step is to issue exactly this Bash tool call.

arguments.command: until ! tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -q "esc to interrupt"; do sleep 3; done; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -14
arguments.description: Wait for essay completion, verify tail visible above input
